title: Wojtek the Soldier Bear

slides.text: Polish soldiers adopted a bear cub named Wojtek. Now the army had to sail to Italy, and animals were not allowed on board.
1944. The solution: make Wojtek a soldier. He was officially enlisted in the 22nd Artillery Supply Company.
He had a name, a rank and a service number. He travelled with the men, rode in their trucks and wrestled with them for fun.
May 1944: the Battle of Monte Cassino in Italy, one of the hardest battles of the war.
Soldiers who were there said Wojtek watched the men work, then began carrying heavy crates of artillery shells himself, and never dropped one.
After the battle, the company made a bear carrying an artillery shell its official badge.

Then the war ended. But what happens to a soldier who is a bear?
Part 3: the final chapter.

caption: To get him onto a troop ship, the army enlisted him. A bear with a rank, a service number and, soldiers said, a job carrying shells at Monte Cassino. Wojtek, part 2 of 3.
